children.help_text:
The listen command watches and forwards webhook events from Stripe to your
local machine by connecting directly to Stripe's API. You can test the latest
API version, filter events, or even load your saved webhook endpoints from your
Stripe account.

Usage:
  stripe listen [flags]

Examples:
  stripe listen
  stripe listen --all-snapshot --forward-to localhost:3000/events
  stripe listen --all-thin --forward-to localhost:3000/events
  stripe listen --events charge.captured,customer.created \
    --forward-to localhost:3000/events
  stripe listen --events v1.billing.meter.no_meter_found \
    --forward-to localhost:3000/events
  stripe listen --all-thin --events-from @accounts \
    --forward-to localhost:3000/events

[Agent guidance]
  Use `--forward-to` to specify where events are sent, e.g. localhost:4242/webhook.
  Use `--events` to filter to specific event types, e.g. `--events checkout.session.completed`.
  Use `--format json` and pipe to `jq` for machine-readable event output.
  Use `--print-secret` to retrieve the webhook signing secret for signature verification.
  If you do not have an account: run stripe sandbox create (provisions a claimable sandbox without a browser).
  If you already have a key: use --api-key (or set STRIPE_API_KEY).
  Nested API fields use bracket flags, e.g. --parent[child]=value, not dotted --parent.child=value.
  Run stripe --map to quickly see all available commands.
  Run stripe resources to discover all available API resources.
  Run stripe

children.help_text:
Log in to your Stripe account to set up the CLI.

By default (when stdin is a terminal), this opens a browser-based login flow: it
prints a pairing code, launches your browser to the Stripe Dashboard, and waits for
you to approve the request before saving your credentials.

Use --interactive when a browser is unavailable:

  --interactive
      Prompts you to paste an API key directly. Useful for SSH sessions or
      CI environments with a human operator.

For agents and scripts, use the two-step non-interactive flow:

  --non-interactive
      Prints a JSON object containing a browser_url, a verification_code to
      confirm the pairing, and a next_step command, then exits immediately.
      Activates automatically when stdin is not a terminal.
      Immediately run the next_step command from the JSON output to poll
      while the user approves in the browser; it blocks until authentication
      completes.

  --complete <poll-url>
      Polls the given URL (from the next_step of a prior --non-interactive run)
      until the user approves in the browser, then saves credentials.

If you're already logged in with a valid session, running this again re-authorizes
the CLI instead: it opens the Stripe Dashboard so you can change permissions or
authorize access to additional accounts or sandboxes. Use --new-session to log out
of the current session and log in as a different user instead. --non-interactive
works here too, printing a browser_url and a next_step of
'stripe login

children.help_text:
Run ad hoc SQL queries against your Stripe data using the Data Reporting API.

Use the query-runs subcommands to kick off a new query and retrieve its
results. This uses the /v2/data/reporting/query_runs Public Preview API.

Usage:
  stripe reporting [command]

Available commands:
  query-runs  Create and retrieve QueryRun objects (Public Preview)

[Agent guidance]
  If you do not have an account: run stripe sandbox create (provisions a claimable sandbox without a browser).
  If you already have a key: use --api-key (or set STRIPE_API_KEY).
  Nested API fields use bracket flags, e.g. --parent[child]=value, not dotted --parent.child=value.
  Run stripe --map to quickly see all available commands.
  Run stripe resources to discover all available API resources.
  Run stripe [resource] --help to see operations and required/common parameters for a resource.
  Run stripe help [resource] [operation] to see the full parameter list for a specific operation.


Flags:
  -h, --help   help for reporting

Global flags:
      --api-key string        Your API key to use for the command, instead
                              of your logged in session. Overridden by the
                              STRIPE_API_KEY environment variable, if set
      --color string          turn on/off color output (on, off, auto)
      --config string         config file (default is
                              $HOME/.config/stripe/config.toml)
